aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate cancer; staging criteria are not specified in the abstract.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: High fish consumption in early- and midlife was not associated with overall or advanced prostate cancer.
study_design: Prospective analysis nested in the AGES-Reykjavik cohort, with dietary assessment in 2002–2006 and follow-up through 2009 using cancer and mortality registers.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The study was nested among 2268 men aged 67-96 years in the AGES-Reykjavik cohort study.
reason: The abstract reports incident overall and advanced prostate cancer analyses. Although it states that 63 cases had advanced disease, that count follows a combined statement about 214 prevalent and 133 incident cases and therefore does not clearly identify the number of incident advanced cases.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Men consuming fish oil in later life had a lower risk of advanced prostate cancer [HR (95%CI): 0.43 (0.19, 0.95)], no association was found for early life or midlife consumption.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate explicitly concerns advanced prostate cancer arising during cohort follow-up.

estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied full-text table evidence places the 0.72 estimate in the total incident prostate cancer columns. The abstract does not report this numeric overall estimate, so endpoint support comes from existing evidence rather than the abstract.
